description: Contextual extensions of existing technique IDs, not a second universal pixel-art rulebook.

lessons.title: Repair the join between foliage masses
lessons.source_observation: Chapter 44 distinguishes modular canopy construction for broadleaf trees and for conifers.
lessons.transfer_decision: Inspect the join between modules; do not increase the number of leaves indiscriminately.
pixel_operations: Mark the region where two canopy groups cross; keep the approved outer contour.
Identify which mass is in front, and join or remove the pixels that contradict that overlap.
Test a variant of the module without its most recognizable mark to detect accidental repetition.
lessons.visual_check: Compare the canopy alone and over its background: does the join describe depth or a seam? Also check that the repair does not produce three disconnected balls.
lessons.counterexample: In a conifer, replacing branch tiers with round bundles changes the species; this procedure does not correct that.

exercise.brief: Build an original tree with an asymmetric canopy and a problematic join.
exercise.comparison: A: initial join; B: localized repair. These are not three design directions.
exercise.question: Which group is in front, and is the canopy's continuity preserved?

lessons.title: Distinguish materials without adding noise
lessons.source_observation: Chapter 43 treats sand and water with different texture constructions.
lessons.transfer_decision: Change the direction and connectivity of pixel clusters before changing their quantity.
pixel_operations: Block in the shape and freeze the palette so that a color change does not hide the problem.
Choose one dominant direction and draw three original motifs, not random dots.
Remove marks from the regions that must stay quiet.
lessons.visual_check: Without animation or labels, compare the materials. Record misreadings; do not declare success because there are fewer isolated pixels.
lessons.counterexample: A stylized material can break its direction; the test evaluates the brief's goal, not mandatory realism.

exercise.brief: Two small original surfaces with an identical color family.
exercise.comparison: A: undifferentiated orientation; B: oriented clusters.
exercise.question: Which one appears to flow, and which one keeps a granular surface?

lessons.title: Validate neighborhoods, not only edges
lessons.source_observation: Chapter 43 proposes observing the connections between variants while building them.
lessons.transfer_decision: Turn the join cases that the map requires into a visible test matrix.
pixel_operations: List the repeated center, edge, convex corner, concave corner, and material join that the runtime actually needs.
Keep base, transition, and decoration in layers if the contract allows them.
Review the cases after each change to the base tile; record the cases not yet built.
lessons.visual_check: View a 3×3 and a mix of neighbors without grid lines. Do not infer continuity because two rows of pixels match.
lessons.counterexample: An intentional paving joint can have a line; it is not automatically an incorrect seam.

exercise.brief: An original base terrain and variants for a concave patch.
exercise.comparison: The same neighborhood before and after repairing the corner.
exercise.question: Can the eye follow the edge without jumps in height or texture?

lessons.authority: Original operational proposal, informed by the listed source sections; not an artist-endorsed rule.

lessons.title: Test the character over difficult backgrounds
lessons.source_observation: Chapters 62 and 63 distinguish the function of the background from the readability of interactive elements.
lessons.transfer_decision: Evaluate the subject at several representative points in the scene, not only over a studio background.
pixel_operations: Freeze the sprite and compare it over light, dark, and textured sectors of the real background.
Choose a single change: redistribute the background values or reinforce a functional region of the subject.
Repeat in color and in values; keep some environmental features so the scene does not lose its character.
lessons.visual_check: Locate the head, support, and tool without relying on a global halo. A less detailed background does not by itself prove better readability.
lessons.counterexample: A game can require camouflage; record it as intent and do not repair it automatically.

exercise.brief: An original scene with a fixed-size character and three test positions.
exercise.comparison: A/B of the background with the same subject and positions.
exercise.question: Can the character be distinguished without the environment losing its depth?

lessons.title: Resolve what top-down means in this brief
lessons.source_observation: Chapter 55 clarifies that its top-down is a 3/4 view that shows top and front surfaces.
lessons.transfer_decision: Name the projection explicitly before choosing a lesson or transferring proportions.
pixel_operations: Distinguish orthographic overhead, oblique RPG top-down, side, and dimetric/isometric.
Draw an original test volume and note which faces can be seen.
Use only compatible references, or describe the required transformation as a new inference.
lessons.visual_check: Compare the top face, front wall, and footprint with the declared camera. The tutorial's name does not decide the camera of the result.
lessons.counterexample: The absence of converging perspective does not turn an oblique view into an overhead view.

exercise.brief: An original box with a declared lid, footprint, and orientation.
exercise.protected: The camera requested by the user.
exercise.comparison: One compatible construction and one camera counterexample.
exercise.question: Does the visible face match the requested camera?

lessons.title: Separate geometric mirroring from lighting
lessons.source_observation: Chapter 6 establishes the light source as part of the construction.
lessons.transfer_decision: Treat geometry reflection and light placement as separate decisions.
pixel_operations: Mirror only the base mask or the appropriate geometric parts.
Reassign planes and contact according to the scene's light source.
Protect asymmetric marks that must not change sides.
lessons.visual_check: Place the original and the mirrored copy in the same scene: do both respond to the same source? Note when the symmetry is deliberate.
lessons.counterexample: If the light belongs to the object and rotates with it, keeping certain highlights can be correct; declare that model.

exercise.brief: Two original rocks or props in a scene with fixed side light.
exercise.comparison: A: mirrored bitmap; B: mirrored mask and redrawn planes.
exercise.question: Does the lit side match the source, without flipping identity details?

lessons.title: Preserve identity across orientations
lessons.source_observation: Chapter 55 distinguishes a symmetric dummy from a character with asymmetric equipment.
lessons.transfer_decision: Record hand, equipment, support, and identity as invariants before delegating the atlas.
pixel_operations: Approve each required base orientation; do not promise eight views from five mirrors without checking the asymmetries.
Compare the position of the support, the head mass, and the equipment side.
Hand off these invariants together with the simplification decisions for animation production.
lessons.visual_check: Inspect rotation and static views. Do not require the same silhouette at every angle; do require the character's continuity.
lessons.counterexample: Some games accept swapping hands for economy. That must be an explicit project concession.

exercise.brief: An original character with a unique shoulder pad and equipment in one hand.
exercise.protected: Equipment side, scale, and support point.
exercise.comparison: Independent front, profile, and back views, not rescaled.
exercise.question: Is it still the same character when it turns?

lessons.title: Separate continuous time from grid drawing
lessons.source_observation: Chapter 63 separates the parallax demonstration from its implementation in an engine with a camera.
lessons.transfer_decision: Keep the temporal simulation and quantize at the agreed presentation point.
pixel_operations: Define the native resolution, the simulation positions, and the rounding rule in draw.
Use elapsed time for displacement, not a speed that depends on the monitor's refresh rate.
Test the loop's end points, pause/resume, and a slow scroll.
lessons.visual_check: Inspect frames to distinguish unavoidable whole-pixel steps from jitter caused by inconsistent rounding. Subjective smoothness still needs observation.
lessons.counterexample: Subpixel motion can be a valid hybrid decision, but it must not be labeled exact-grid.

exercise.brief: An original background with two scrolling layers and a reference marker.
exercise.comparison: The same path with consistent quantization and with inconsistent rounding.
exercise.question: Does each art pixel keep its size, and does each layer close its loop?

lessons.title: Check blends against the palette contract
lessons.source_observation: Chapter 43 includes a water transition with opacity blending.
lessons.transfer_decision: Separate an artistic option from the tutorial from a contract that requires a strict final palette.
pixel_operations: Declare whether the budget applies to the sprite, to the layers, or to the final composite.
In strict mode, authorize a table of blend colors or redraw the transition with existing colors.
Review the composite over the target backgrounds, in addition to the asset's RGBA.
lessons.visual_check: Counting colors verifies the technical contract, not whether the water looks convincing. Record both reviews separately.
lessons.counterexample: A hybrid scene can allow new compositing colors; do not quantize it without authorization.

exercise.brief: Two original states of a translucent surface.
exercise.comparison: Free blending versus a transition within the declared palette.
exercise.question: Was the budget respected without destroying the read of the material?

lessons.title: Distribute detail by distance and function
lessons.source_observation: Chapter 62 relates detail and depth bands to the context of each landscape.
lessons.transfer_decision: Give each band a visual job and remove detail that cannot be read at that distance.
pixel_operations: Fix the horizon, the main occlusions, and the usable region for the action.
Reduce the size or presence of distant marks according to the apparent distance.
Compare a values version before recoloring the whole landscape.
lessons.visual_check: Can the foreground, middle ground, and background be ordered? Keep enough information to tell two nearby planes apart.
lessons.counterexample: Always darkening distant areas or always lightening them are wrong recipes: night, backlight, and fog change the case.

exercise.brief: An original landscape with three distances and an area for a character.
exercise.comparison: The same scene with a uniform and with a hierarchical distribution of detail.
exercise.question: Does the depth read without erasing the elements that identify the place?

lessons.title: Check the scaling arithmetic
lessons.source_observation: Chapter 63 contains a discrepancy between native resolution, factor, and output resolution.
lessons.transfer_decision: Calculate the dimensions; separate scaling, margins, and cropping in the contract.
pixel_operations: Calculate width×factor and height×factor with integers.
If the container differs, declare letterboxing or change the resolution through a decision in the brief.
Also verify DPR and browser zoom; integer CSS scale does not by itself guarantee the physical grid.
lessons.visual_check: 470×240 at 4× gives 1880×960. 480×270 at 4× gives 1920×1080. Do not attribute an unpublished correction to the author.
lessons.counterexample: A 1920×1080 container with 1880×960 art and margins can be valid; it is not an exact stretch.

exercise.brief: Declare a render contract for a self-contained HTML file.
exercise.comparison: Calculation of the native surface, render, and container.
exercise.question: Is the art stretched, or does the grid hold with explicit margins?

lessons.title: Show what the texture contributes
symptoms: mucho detalle pero se ve mal
lessons.source_observation: Chapters 5 and 44 give weight to the order of pixel clusters, not only to low resolution.
lessons.transfer_decision: Use a texture ablation to check whether the material rests on resolved forms.
pixel_operations: Export the same construction without texture and without changing the silhouette or planes.
Reintroduce only the marks that help a required feature.
Keep the before/after and the edited region, without calling every pixel reduction an improvement.
lessons.visual_check: Compare volume, material, and identity separately. The cleaner version can lose necessary texture and must not win by default.
lessons.counterexample: Strong texture can define the style. The question is what it communicates, not how minimal it looks. Do not remove eyes, functional highlights, or costume patterns that are identity signals. A preference for a clean piece does not invalidate a textured style.

exercise.brief: An original object with texture, a plane base, and an identity feature.
exercise.comparison: Material ablation, followed by selective reintroduction.
exercise.question: Which mark improves material or identity, and which one only distracts?
